messages.author: 2f095572d08a899f
messages.subject: MIMIC model error
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to run mimic model, but R keeps giving me an error.

Following is the code I used:
mimic.model <- '
  #measurement model
  AUDfactor =~ S1+S2+S3+S4+S5+S6+S7+S8+S9+S10+S11
  #regressions
  AUDfactor ~ PRS + age + sex + PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5
  S1 ~ PRS
'
fit2 <- sem(model = mimic.model, data = merge)
summary(fit2, standardized = T)
fitMeasures(fit2, c("cfi", "rmsea", "srmr"))

Following is the error message I got:
"Model estimation FAILED! Returning starting values." for "fit2 <- sem(model = mimic.model, data = merge)"
** WARNING ** Estimates below are simply the starting values for "summary(fit2, standardized = T)"
"Error in lav_fit_measures(object = object, fit.measures = fit.measures, : lavaan ERROR: fit measures not available if model did not converge" for "fitMeasures(fit2, c("cfi", "rmsea", "srmr"))"

To be exact, I am trying to test the effect of 'PRS' on "S1" after controlling for "AUDfactor" in mimic model. I have attached the plot to help understanding. What should I do to fix this?

Thank you all.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: MIMIC model error
parts:
This may be a scaling problem. What about using a different scaling
indicator;

AUDfactor =~ S2 + S1 + S3 + ...

If you can send me the dataset, I can investigate more.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: MIMIC model error
parts:
It was a scaling problem indeed. The variance of PRS is 1.517004e-15! All values are around 1e-06. Multiplying these values with a fixed constant (say, 1e07) will fix the problem:

library(lavaan)

library(openxlsx)
Data <- read.xlsx("merge.xlsx")
names(Data)[18] <- "sex"
Data$PRS2 <- Data$PRS * 1e07
dim(Data)

AUDfactor ~ PRS2 + age + sex + PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5
   S1 ~ PRS2
'
fit <- sem(model = mimic.model, data = Data)

On Tuesday, November 22, 2022 at 11:13:56 AM UTC+1 Yves Rosseel wrote:
This may be a scaling problem. What about using a different scaling
indicator;

AUDfactor =~ S2 + S1 + S3 + ...

If you can send me the dataset, I can investigate more.

Yves.
